reason: A May 9 report citing Dainik Jagran identifies Sanju Samson as the selection committee's frontrunner to take over India's T20I captaincy for the upcoming Ireland and England series. Incumbent Suryakumar Yadav remains a substantial alternative because the report explicitly says he may retain the role for those series, but Samson's Player-of-the-Tournament run and likely deputy role make him the new favorite.

FIFA granted Ange-Yoan Bonny's switch from France to Ivory Coast on May 8. Reuters specifically says he is expected in the World Cup squad and could debut in the exact June 4 friendly against France, while noting his productive super-sub role for Inter. That unusually direct match linkage makes Bonny the leading candidate for the decisive Ivory Coast goal.

Bonny's newly granted nationality switch, expected World Cup selection and late addition to the Ivorian player pool make him the clearest administrative-status candidate for the later Canada entry-authorization question. The May 9 report confirms FIFA eligibility rather than Canadian immigration approval, so established forwards retain meaningful probability.

Jorge Martin won the May 9 French sprint and closed to six points behind championship leader Marco Bezzecchi. Francesco Bagnaia took pole after a setup breakthrough, while Marc Marquez fractured his right foot, required surgery and will miss France and Catalunya after sitting 51 points off the lead. Bagnaia enters the Czech-race top five and Marquez is cut materially, though the June 21 horizon allows recovery.

Bruno Fernandes remains favorite after winning the closely related FWA award. Manchester City's May 9 win moved the club within two points of Arsenal and Erling Haaland scored his 26th league goal, modestly strengthening Haaland's official Premier League award path while slightly reducing Fernandes and Rice.
